title: Xamarin and MAUI
cards/0/title: Xamarin: C# for iOS and Android
cards/0/body:
Xamarin (2011) let you write mobile apps in C# and share code between iOS and Android. At first it cost money, and quite a lot of it.

In 2016 Microsoft bought Xamarin and made it free.
cards/1/task: Find the year Microsoft bought Xamarin. What else big happened that year?
cards/2/body:
Xamarin.Forms gave you one XAML UI for every platform. In 2022 it was replaced by .NET MAUI: the same approach, but on modern .NET, plus Windows and macOS.

Xamarin support ended in May 2024.
cards/3/title: Native controls vs drawing it yourself
cards/3/body:
MAUI turns your button into a real iOS or Android button: native controls. It looks and feels native, but differs slightly on each platform.

Avalonia draws everything itself, like a game: pixel-identical everywhere. More on that in the Avalonia course.
cards/4/q: How does MAUI's approach differ from Avalonia's?
cards/4/options/0: MAUI uses the platform's native controls, Avalonia draws the UI itself
cards/4/explain: Hence the trade-off: MAUI looks native, Avalonia looks the same everywhere.
cards/6/q: Match each technology to what it is
cards/6/pairs/0/1: C# on iOS and Android, built on Mono
cards/7/q: What is true? Select all that apply.
cards/7/options/3: MAUI is the new version of WPF
cards/7/explain: WPF is a separate, Windows-only technology.
